chunks: A group narrated for Abi Muhammad Harun ibn Musa al-Talakbari, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, from Hanzala ibn Zakariya, from the reliable one, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Abbas al-Alawi narrated to me—and I have not seen anyone more truthful in speech than him, and he differed with us in many matters—who said: Abu al-Fadl al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi narrated to me, saying: I entered upon Abi Muhammad (peace be upon him) in Sarra al-Manna and congratulated him on our Master, the Master of the Age (peace be upon him), upon his birth.

key_terms.الثِّقَة: The reliable one (a specific narrator or title)
key_terms.بِسَرِّ مَنِىَّ: In Sarra al-Manna (a city in Iraq)
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الزَّمَانِ: Master of the Age (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: Who congratulated Imam al-Askari on the birth of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the historical reality of the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him) during the Minor Ghaiba, specifically noting the congratulation offered to Imam al-Hasn al-Askari (peace be upon him). The inclusion of Abdullah ibn al-Abbas al-Alawi, a prominent figure who differed with the Shia in some theological matters yet was deemed trustworthy (*thiqa*), underscores the widespread acceptance of the Imam's birth across various sects. This narration serves as a foundational evidence for the continuity of the Imamate and the legitimacy of the Twelfth Imam's lineage.
